rights: You have the right to remain silent (5th Amendment)
You must provide license, registration, and proof of insurance if driving
You have the right to refuse consent to a vehicle search (4th Amendment)
You have the right to record the encounter in public
You can ask 'Am I free to go?' to determine if you are being detained
You do not have to answer questions about where you are going or coming from
de_escalation_tips: Keep your hands visible on the steering wheel
Turn on interior lights if it is dark
Do not reach for documents until asked
Stay calm and speak politely
Do not physically resist even if you believe the stop is unlawful
Say 'I exercise my right to remain silent' clearly if you choose not to answer

rights: You have the right to remain silent (5th Amendment)
You can ask 'Am I being detained or am I free to go?'
You do not have to consent to a search of your person or belongings
You have the right to record the encounter
In most states, you are not required to show ID unless you are being detained
You have the right to walk away if you are not being detained
de_escalation_tips: Stay calm and keep your hands visible
Do not run or make sudden movements
Politely ask if you are being detained
If you are free to go, calmly walk away
Do not physically resist a pat-down; verbally state you do not consent

rights: You do not have to open the door unless officers have a warrant
Ask to see the warrant through a window or slid under the door
A warrant must specify the correct address and be signed by a judge
You have the right to remain silent
You do not have to consent to a search of your home
You have the right to record inside your own home
de_escalation_tips: Speak through a closed door if possible
Ask to see identification and badge numbers
Ask 'Do you have a warrant?' before opening
If they have a valid warrant, do not physically resist entry
State clearly 'I do not consent to a search' if no warrant

rights: You have the right to peacefully protest in public spaces (1st Amendment)
You have the right to photograph and record in public
You do not need a permit for small groups on public sidewalks
You have the right to remain silent if questioned
Police cannot confiscate or demand to see your photos/videos without a warrant
You have the right to legal representation if arrested
de_escalation_tips: Stay in public areas where you have the right to be
Keep your hands visible and avoid sudden movements
Follow lawful dispersal orders to avoid arrest
Document badge numbers and officer names
Have an emergency contact ready

rights: You have the right to remain silent regardless of immigration status
You do not have to discuss your immigration status with local police
You have the right to speak to an attorney
ICE agents must have a judicial warrant to enter your home
You do not have to sign any documents without speaking to a lawyer
You have the right to make a phone call if detained
de_escalation_tips: Stay calm and do not run
Do not provide false documents
Say 'I wish to remain silent and speak to a lawyer'
Do not sign anything you do not understand
Carry your attorney's contact information

rights: You have the right to remain silent (5th Amendment)
You have the right to refuse consent to searches (4th Amendment)
You have the right to an attorney (6th Amendment)
You have the right to record police in public
You have the right to know why you are being detained
de_escalation_tips: Stay calm and keep your hands visible
Be polite but firm about your rights
Do not physically resist
Remember badge numbers and patrol car numbers
Request a supervisor if you feel your rights are being violated
